$comment: Lab energy-pipe graph (ADR-0004), shared by the TS EnergyNetwork and the native --mode energy-network smoke. Regenerate: npm run codegen:constants. Allocation along these pipes is simulated accounting, not metrology. An edge either states maxWatts (the original classroom graph) or names a device whose physics/constants.json energyNetwork.deviceNameplateWatts entry becomes its capacity; codegen fails on a nameplate that does not exist, so a pipe is skipped rather than given an invented watt. The field (ADR-0011) and charge (ADR-0013) buses are separate graphs on separate switches and do not live here.

energyPipes.note: Classroom path: transformer → Halbach → homopolar → SEG metaphor.
The MHD channel generates, the rail sled consumes the same I×B physics as a motor.
Mutual inductance as coupled L-M phasors, then the same coupling doing mechanical work on a shorted secondary.
A Faraday disc is the textbook low-voltage, high-current source; the Hall strip wants about an ampere at a fraction of a volt. Capacity is the Hall bench nameplate.
The belt motor runs off the bench supply. Capacity is the VdG nameplate — the motor's draw, not the watts reaching the sphere (microamps at ~100 kV is well under a watt).

The capacitor bank recharges between shots. Capacity is the pulse-coil nameplate, C·V²/(4τ) from physics/constants.json pulseCoil — the peak power of its exponential recharge, so a ceiling on the average draw, not the joules in one shot.
